title: Ground reference data error and the mis-estimation of the area of land cover change as a function of its abundance
relevance: Shows that the mis-estimation of CHANGE area caused by reference error depends on how ABUNDANT the change class is, and change classes are always rare - which is the trap our whole change product sits in. With canopy loss at a few percent of pixels, a small false-positive rate on the vast unchanged population can rival or exceed the true signal: at 97% specificity roughly half of all detected change would be spurious. Our per-year precision is measured on the CANOPY class (.77-.96), but nobody has measured specificity on the UNCHANGED class across an epoch pair, and that is the quantity governing a change product. This is the third Foody paper in the tracker (IDs 79, 87) and together they define our reference-error problem.

title: Impact of error on landscape pattern analyses performed on land-cover change maps (misclassification error propagation in land cover change categorization)
relevance: Treats misclassification error propagation specifically in land cover CHANGE categorization, and finds spatio-temporal interdependence matters: naive variance and covariance propagation, which assumes independent per-date errors, yields biased standard errors. Directly relevant because our change product is built by comparing independently produced per-year masks whose errors are certainly correlated in space and across dates - the same model, the same blind spot, the same ground. Means our change uncertainty cannot be obtained by simply combining per-year accuracy figures, which is the obvious thing to do and would understate it.
